SPECIFICATION FOR 
WROUGHT ALUMINIUM UTENSILS 

PART VI COMPARTMENTAL TRAYS 



1. Scope — Specifies shapes, dimensions and other requirements for compartmental trays made of 

aluminium. 

2. Material — The aluminium used for the manufacture of trays shall conform to IS : 21-1975 * Speci- 
fication for wrought aluminium and aluminium alloys for manufacture of utensils {third revision y. 

3. Grades — The compartmer^tai trays shall be of two grades as given below; depending upon the 
thickness of sheet used; 

Grade Tliickness of Sheet 

Standard grade r60 mm 

Utiliiy grade 1-25 mm 

4. Shapes and Dimensions 

4*1 Typicai shapes of compartmental trays are shown in Fig. 1 to 3. The number, shapes and 
dimensions of compartments may be altered to suit the requirements of the purchaser. The compart- 
mental trays of any one type and of one manufacturer shall be so made as to nest in one another so 
that these may be staci^ed in a limited space. 

4.2 The dimensions of the compartmental trays shall be as given in Fig. 1 to 3, The dimensions 
shall have the foliowing tolerances: 

Dimensions 

Over Up to and Including 

mm mm 

50 

50 100 

100 200 

200 - 

4.3 The reduction in thickness of compartmental trays after draw shall not exceed O'SO mm. 

5. Workmanship and Finish 

5.1 lVor;(/r?ans/)/p - Compartmental trays shall be pressed in one piece. The compartments shall 
be well defined and of good shape. Their corners shall be suitably radiused. The top edges of the 
compartments and the rim of the trays shall be in one plane and the bottoms shall also lie in one 
plane. The edges of the trays shall be rounded or suitably bent over to th^ underside. When bent 
over, they shall be ^o pressed as not to leave any crevice. 

5.2 The trays shall be finished bright all over. These may also be anodized. If anodized, these shall 
conform to Grade AC5 of IS : 1868-1968 'Specification for anodic coatings on aluminium 
{first revision) \ The pressing of the trays shall be such that they shall be cleanable thoroughly by 
ordinary method of cleaning by hand, brush or scrub. The trays shall be free from distortionT dents' 
wrinkles, scratches, pittings, deep tool marks, and other surface defects.

IS: 1660 ( Part VI )- 1980 

6. Marking - Each tray shall be suitably marked at the bottom with the manufacturer's name, trade- 
mark or identification mark and the corresponding grade. The impression of the marking shall not 
show up on the inside. 

6.1 ISI Certification Marking -Details available with the Indian Standards Instrtution. 

7. Packing — Trays shall be packed in accordance wrth the best trade practices. Care shall be 
taken to see that the trays do not get dented during transit. 

8. Sampling — The sampling of trays shall be done in accordance with IS : 9040- 1978 ' Methods for 
sampling of utensils '.

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was earlier published as IS : 4136-1968. ' Specification for aluminium compart- 
menial trays \ In this revision, the standard has been redesignated as a part of Indian Standards on 
wrought aluminium utensils in order to facilitate its implementation. The requirements pertaining 
to grading of trays anti sampling have also been included. 

For Railway applications, a cover may be required to be used with compartmental trays. Its 
specifications will be as per agreement between the purchaser and the supplier till separate require- 
ments are laid down for covers.
